dependencies.description: Unlike strfHEADER (line 117), strnHEADER (line 154), JUNKHEADER (line 228) and genericblock (line 165), the strfHEADER_WAVE definition at lines 143-146 has no 'if (datalen % 2)' branch. Keep the audio format chunk's datalen even (18, 20, 30, 40 ...).

dependencies.then: every multi-byte field in the whole file must be big-endian, and the template calls BigEndian() from that point on
dependencies.description: Line 257 tests id[3] == 'X' and line 260 switches the byte order for all subsequent reads (the else branch calls LittleEndian() at line 265). Mainstream demuxers accept only 'RIFF', which is why ROOT.id is pinned.

dependencies.when: genericblock.id begins with the two ASCII digits NN
dependencies.then: a LIST 'strl' declaring stream NN must appear earlier in the file, and the sample must be well-formed for that stream's codec
dependencies.description: FFmpeg's get_stream_idx() maps the digit pair to a stream index and drops the chunk when no such stream exists, so the sample never reaches a decoder.

dependencies.then: an 'idx1' chunk must be present, conventionally as the last top-level chunk, holding 16 * n bytes for the n movi chunks it indexes
dependencies.description: Advertising an index that is absent makes index-driven readers fail their lookup and fall back to a sequential scan, or refuse the file; the flag and the chunk must agree.

dependencies.then: the demuxer switches to its non-interleaved chunk-reordering path and buffers chunks per stream instead of reading them in file order
dependencies.description: This is a genuinely different function body in the demuxer, so clearing the bit is a coverage choice, not an error - but the movi layout should then be grouped per stream to be coherent.

dependencies.then: '##pc' palette-change chunks may appear in movi, each carrying 4 * palette_entries RGBQUADs
dependencies.description: The flag is what tells the reader to expect mid-stream palette updates and to run its palette-change handling branch.

dependencies.then: ckid must be the fourcc 'LIST' and dwChunkOffset / dwChunkLength must describe a LIST 'rec ' record group rather than a single sample
dependencies.description: A record-group index entry points at a container, not at a media chunk; mixing the two makes the index resolve to the wrong bytes.

dependencies.when: any chunk in the file has an odd datalen
dependencies.then: exactly one 0x00 pad byte must follow its payload, and that pad byte is not counted in datalen but is counted by every offset and by LISTHEADER.datalen
dependencies.description: RIFF requires chunks to start on even offsets. The template models this in strfHEADER (line 117), strnHEADER (line 154), genericblock (line 165) and JUNKHEADER (line 228) by reading datalen+1 bytes, and its sizeof()-based advances depend on the pad being present.

structure.subject: ROOT (RIFF form head)
structure.detail: The file must begin with the 12-byte RIFF head: 'RIFF', uint32 datalen, 'AVI '. The template instantiates ROOT first (line 280) and aborts with Warning("Not a valid AVI file") plus return -1 if the form type is not 'AVI ' (lines 271-274). Byte order for everything after this head is selected by ROOT.id (LittleEndian at line 265, BigEndian at line 260).
structure.output_budget: n/a - single fixed 12-byte head, never repeated

structure.subject: top-level chunk sequence after the RIFF head
structure.detail: A flat sequence of chunks walked by the loop at lines 282-303. Canonical AVI order is LIST 'hdrl' first, then LIST 'movi', then 'idx1' last; 'JUNK' padding and other LIST forms ('INFO', 'odml', 'Tdat') may appear anywhere. The template accepts only the three ids LIST, JUNK and idx1 at this level.
structure.output_budget: running total of top-level chunk bytes (8 + datalen + pad each), capped at 64 KiB and checked before each OPTIONAL chunk is added; the mandatory LIST 'hdrl' and LIST 'movi' are always emitted within it. Rationale: the interesting structure of an AVI is its header lists plus its sample payloads, and 64 KiB keeps each generated file small enough to be decoded thousands of times per campaign while still leaving room for several strl lists, a 32 KiB movi, JUNK padding and a complete idx1 - with no field anywhere narrowed to achieve it.

structure.subject: LIST 'hdrl'
structure.detail: Exactly one main header list must be present, and it must come before LIST 'movi' so that stream parameters are known before the samples. Its type fourcc must be 'hdrl' for the template to take the avih branch (line 179).
structure.output_budget: n/a - one fixed list; its own budget is bounded by the strl budget below

structure.subject: avihHEADER inside LIST 'hdrl'
structure.detail: The first chunk inside LIST 'hdrl' must be 'avih' holding a 56-byte MainAVIHeader. The template reads it unconditionally and reads nothing else from the hdrl branch (line 181), then lets the top-level loop re-dispatch each nested LIST 'strl'.
structure.output_budget: n/a - single fixed 64-byte chunk (id + datalen + 56), never repeated

structure.subject: LIST 'strl' per stream
structure.detail: One LIST 'strl' per stream, nested inside LIST 'hdrl' after the avih chunk, conventionally in stream-index order (00, 01, 02 ...). At least one stream is required for the file to carry media. The template parses each strl as strh + strf + strn (lines 185-200) and the top-level loop finds each nested strl because it too begins with 'LIST'.
structure.output_budget: at most 8 strl lists and 4 KiB of strl bytes total, accumulated as each list is emitted; rationale: 4 KiB covers an 8 bpp stream's 1024-byte palette plus framing for several streams, so palette-heavy files fit without capping biWidth, biHeight, biBitCount or biClrUsed - those stay free and the palette size follows from them.

structure.subject: contents of one LIST 'strl'
structure.detail: In order: 'strh' with a 56-byte AVIStreamHeader, then the 'strf' chunk whose structure is selected exclusively by fccType (BITMAPINFOHEADER for 'vids', WAVEFORMATEX for 'auds', opaque otherwise), then 'strn' with the stream name. The template reads all three unconditionally, so 'strn' is mandatory here even though the AVI spec makes it optional.
structure.output_budget: counted against the strl budget above; one strl list is 64 + (8 + strf datalen + pad) + (8 + strn datalen + pad) bytes

structure.subject: strfHEADER_BIH / strfHEADER_WAVE / strfHEADER
structure.detail: Exactly one of the three strf structures is instantiated per stream, chosen by AVIStreamHeader.fccType: 'vids' -> strfHEADER_BIH (line 190), 'auds' -> strfHEADER_WAVE (line 194), anything else -> generic strfHEADER (line 198). A stream cannot carry two format chunks and the choice is not free once fccType is fixed.
structure.output_budget: n/a - single fixed choice per stream

structure.subject: LIST 'movi'
structure.detail: Exactly one media data list, after LIST 'hdrl'. Its type fourcc must be 'movi' for the template to take the sample-walk branch (line 202). Without it the file declares streams but carries no samples, so no decoder does any real work.
structure.output_budget: see the movi data-chunk entry below; this list is the single structure that receives the file's payload budget (32 KiB of sample data)

structure.subject: genericblock data chunks inside LIST 'movi'
structure.detail: One or more media chunks, each 8 + datalen (+ 1 pad byte when odd). The template's do-while loop (lines 209-214) always reads at least one block, so an empty movi list is not representable here. Chunk ids are '##dc'/'##db'/'##wb'/... naming the owning stream; the order in which different streams' chunks interleave is entirely free, which is what AVIF_ISINTERLEAVED advertises.
structure.output_budget: at most 32 KiB of movi data (LISTHEADER.datalen - 4), accumulated as 8 + datalen + pad per chunk and checked before each new sample is emitted; rationale: this is where the real payload lives so it takes half the file budget - 32 KiB holds dozens of small frames or a few larger ones, and the FRAME COUNT follows from the free dimensions (biWidth, biHeight, biBitCount) and the free per-frame size rather than being capped itself. Total file size is controlled here, never by narrowing a Tier C field.

structure.subject: movi sub-chunk tiling
structure.detail: The sub-chunks must tile LISTHEADER.datalen - 4 bytes exactly, back to back, with their pad bytes included and no gaps or slack: the loop terminates on pointer != stop becoming false (line 214) where stop = datalen - 4 (line 205) and pointer accumulates sizeof(gb) (line 212). A single byte of slack sends the template past the end of the list.
structure.output_budget: shared with the movi data-chunk budget above (32 KiB)

structure.subject: RIFF pad byte after any odd-length chunk payload
structure.detail: Every chunk whose datalen is odd must be followed by exactly one 0x00 pad byte, which is NOT counted in datalen but IS counted by every enclosing length and offset. The template models this in strfHEADER (line 117), strnHEADER (line 154), genericblock (line 165) and JUNKHEADER (line 228) by reading datalen+1 bytes. The exception is strfHEADER_WAVE (lines 143-146), which has no parity branch, so its datalen must be even.
structure.output_budget: n/a - at most one byte per odd-length chunk

structure.subject: top-level chunk ids other than LIST, JUNK and idx1
structure.detail: The template's top-level dispatch compares the four bytes it read ahead against exactly 'LIST' (line 286), 'JUNK' (line 290) and 'idx1' (line 294); any other id reaches the else branch at line 298, prints 'unknown chunk' (line 301) and returns -1 (line 302), ending the parse. In particular OpenDML's top-level 'AVIX' extension forms, 'ix##'/'xx##' super-index chunks, 'vprp' and a bare 'dmlh' are unusable at this level - they must be wrapped in a LIST (e.g. LIST 'odml' holding 'dmlh') to survive.
structure.output_budget: n/a - no bytes may be emitted for these ids

structure.subject: idx1HEADER
structure.detail: The legacy index is optional but, when present, conventionally follows LIST 'movi' as the last top-level chunk. Its id must be 'idx1' (line 294) and its body is a whole number of 16-byte AVIINDEXENTRY records (line 250). Writers reserve space for it with a leading JUNK chunk and backfill it at the end.
structure.output_budget: at most 8 KiB of index data (512 entries of 16 bytes); rationale: the index grows with the number of movi samples, which the movi budget already bounds, so this cap only prevents pathological backfill-style files with thousands of padding entries.

structure.subject: JUNKHEADER padding chunks
structure.detail: Zero or more, anywhere at the top level (and legal inside movi). Content is unchecked; only datalen and the pad byte matter. JUNK is a free magnitude axis that shifts every subsequent offset, which makes it valuable for exercising offset arithmetic in the index and the demuxer.
structure.output_budget: at most 8 KiB of padding total across all JUNK chunks, accumulated per chunk; rationale: enough to move idx1 and movi to interesting offsets and to exercise odd/even alignment, without letting padding dominate a 64 KiB file.

structure.subject: idx1 entry count and datalen
structure.detail: idx1HEADER.datalen must be exactly 16 * number_of_entries (AVIINDEXENTRYLEN, line 244), because the template indexes the body with integer division data[datalen/AVIINDEXENTRYLEN] (line 250) - a non-multiple leaves unread bytes that desynchronise the top-level walk. For a coherent file the entries cover every media chunk in movi, one per chunk, in file order.
structure.output_budget: counted against the 8 KiB idx1 budget above

structure.subject: LIST 'hdrl' versus LIST 'movi' versus 'idx1'
structure.detail: hdrl must precede movi (stream parameters are needed before samples are dispatched to a decoder), and idx1 must follow movi because its offsets refer to movi chunks. JUNK and metadata LISTs have no positional requirement.
structure.output_budget: n/a - ordering rule, no bytes of its own

structure.subject: avihHEADER
structure.detail: Exactly one per file, as the first chunk of LIST 'hdrl'. A second 'avih' would be parsed by this template as a stray top-level chunk and rejected (lines 298-302).

structure.subject: chunks inside one LIST 'strl'
structure.detail: strh, strf and strn sit back to back with their pad bytes and must fill LISTHEADER.datalen - 4 exactly; the template reads them as three consecutive struct instances (lines 185-200) with no length checking of its own, so any slack appears as a bogus next-chunk id.
structure.output_budget: counted against the 4 KiB strl budget above

diversity_axes.why: Frame width sets the DIB row stride, the codec's macroblock alignment, the scaler's inner loop counts and the size of every video sample; it is the single strongest size axis in AVI and pinning it would collapse all of them.

Frame height multiplies the stride into the sample size, and its sign additionally selects the top-down versus bottom-up row order in every raw-video decoder - two independent branches that a single pinned value would delete.

Pixel depth chooses between the palettised, 16-bit-mask, 24-bit and 32-bit unpacking paths and decides whether a palette must be present in strf; it is Tier B (enumerated) precisely so that all eight legal depths stay reachable rather than only 24.

This fourcc selects the video decoder itself - raw, MJPEG, MPEG-4, YUV planar/packed, RLE, H.263/AVC - so it is the axis that decides which decoder function bodies run at all; the full registered tag set must stay available.
Palette entry count: it decides how many RGBQUADs the strf chunk must carry and how the decoder's palette-expansion loop runs, and 0 versus an explicit count is a distinct branch.
The file-level display width, which decoders reconcile against biWidth; a disagreement is itself a branch, so it must not be forced to equal biWidth.
The file-level display height; same reconciliation branch as dwWidth and the same reason to leave it free.

Six independent AVIF_* flags switch whole demuxer behaviours (index use, interleaved versus per-stream buffering, chunk-size trust, capture-file provenance); every OR-subset is legal and each is a different code path.
Declared frame count versus the count actually present in movi: the mismatch case is a real reconciliation branch in demuxers, and capping it would tie file size to a constant.

Number of streams is the strongest structural axis in AVI (video only, audio only, video+audio, multi-audio, with text); it is declared freely here and realised by emitting that many LIST 'strl' chunks within the strl output_budget.
Frame duration: drives timestamp generation, frame-rate reduction and the fallback path to dwRate/dwScale when it is zero. Free magnitudes exercise the duration arithmetic without any gate.
Denominator of the file clock; only the ratio to dwRate matters, so any pair is legal and extreme pairs exercise the fraction-reduction and overflow guards.
Numerator of the file clock; together with dwScale it fixes the nominal frame rate and therefore which timing branch runs.
Stream type selects the strf parser inside this template (lines 188, 192, 198) and the whole subsystem in a real demuxer; all five registered types must stay reachable.
Names the compressor/decompressor for the stream and is the fallback codec selector when biCompression is BI_RGB; an open fourcc registry means an open set of decoder entry points.
AVISF_DISABLED and AVISF_VIDEO_PALCHANGES each switch a demuxer branch (skip stream, expect '##pc' palette updates); four combinations, all legal.
Per-stream sample count: a count field, so it is exactly the kind of value that must never be ranged; the real count comes from the movi chunks the generator emits within the movi budget.
Per-stream time unit; for audio it is conventionally 1 with dwRate = nSamplesPerSec, for video a frame duration - two different timestamp paths worth reaching.
Per-stream clock numerator; paired with dwScale it fixes sample timestamps and therefore the A/V sync branch.

Audio codec selector: PCM, float, A-law/mu-law, the ADPCM family, GSM, MP3, WMA, EXTENSIBLE and the degenerate UNKNOWN/DEVELOPMENT values each open a different audio decoder or a different failure path.
Channel count drives interleaving, the channel-map branches and the mixer/resampler path; mono, stereo, 5.1 and 7.1 are all separate code paths.
Sample width selects the PCM unpacking routine and the integer-versus-float path; all nine legal widths must stay reachable, including the awkward 0, 4, 12, 20 and 64.
Sample rate decides the resampler path, the audio frame duration and the ADPCM/MP3 block-size tables; free rates reach branches a fixed 44100 never would.

Chunk fourcc encodes both the stream index and the sample kind ('dc' compressed, 'db' uncompressed, 'wb' audio, 'pc' palette change, 'tc' timecode, 'tx' text); it is the axis that decides the interleave pattern across streams and which dispatch branch runs per chunk.

Per-sample size: derived from the free dimensions and the codec, so it needs no range of its own, and the NUMBER of samples is bounded only by the movi output_budget. This is the field a size-conscious author would be tempted to pin to one frame - it must stay derived and free.

The media sample payload: its contents are free within the codec's own well-formedness rules, and its size follows from biWidth/biHeight/biBitCount or from the codec. It is the payload_wellformedness entry, so nothing about it may be narrowed to make generation easier.

Form type selects the container meaning: hdrl, strl, movi and rec have real handlers, while INFO, odml, Tdat, IDIT and JUNK exercise the metadata and opaque-body paths - all legal, all different code.
Which chunk each index entry names: mirroring the movi fourccs keeps the index resolvable, while 'LIST' entries point at record groups - a different seek path. Free within the pattern.
Keyframe, list-group, first/last and no-time flags each select a branch in index loading and seeking; six atomic flags means 64 legal combinations and every one is worth emitting.

Padding size is a free magnitude that shifts every following chunk offset, so it exercises offset arithmetic in the demuxer and the index and the odd/even alignment paths - bounded only by the JUNK output_budget, never by a field range.
Free-form stream name text of arbitrary (odd or even) length: the characters are metadata and the length additionally exercises the RIFF pad-byte path.
